title: The end of the world has your name on a form
dek: Twelve questions about what you'd actually do when the warning hits. No survival knowledge needed; the form fills itself in.

questions.prompt: Your phone goes off at 4am. What does the alert say?

options.label: Six minutes, then a shockwave
The grid is down and it isn't coming back
The water is already at the end of the street
Nothing dramatic. Deliveries just stopped

questions.prompt: The evacuation order. You follow it how?

options.label: North, to somewhere cold and empty
Inland and uphill, immediately
Nowhere. Seal the doors and wait
Whoever is still sending coordinates
Loud, fast, over before lunch
Slow, quiet, deniable for years

questions.prompt: The view from your window on day one:

options.label: A dark sky over water that has come too far
options.alt: A dark storm cloud over a stony shore

options.label: A street with the lights off, all the way down
Dry ground where there used to be fields
Smoke on the horizon and no wind to move it
options.alt: A dark building under a heavy storm sky

questions.prompt: Plot where you'd be when it settles.
questions.helper: Across: stay and organise, or move and don't look back. Up: underground, or into the cold.

questions.prompt: Rank the infrastructure you'd save first.
questions.helper: First place is the one you'd defend with your body.

questions.prompt: The message you leave on the group chat.
questions.helper: Two gaps. It's 4am; grammar is optional.
questions.template: When it happens I'll be {a}, because {b}.

options.label: already packed and heading north
checking on everyone I know
offline and unreachable
outside watching the sky
someone has to keep the lights on
I've read the projections
there's nothing else to do
the machines are already ahead of us

questions.prompt: If it comes to it, I'd rather vanish than be rescued.
I'd take a disaster I can see coming over one I can't.
Civilisation is held together by supply chains, not by people.
Day thirty. The thing that actually gets you:

options.label: The cold, at night, in your hands
The water, eventually
The quiet
Something that thinks faster than you

questions.prompt: The version of the end you'd genuinely pick:

options.label: One bright flash, then nothing to worry about
The machines take over and are frankly better at it
The sea takes the coast back, slowly
A fever, then empty streets, then quiet

results.name: The Fallout Shelter
results.tagline: Sealed, stocked, not opening for a year
results.blurb: You are the person who reads the whole warning before moving, and by then everyone else has taken the good road. You have water, a radio and a plan with dates on it. Your disaster is the one where patience is the entire skill, and you have patience to spare.
strengths: Genuinely prepared for the boring part
results.watchOut: A sealed door also keeps out the people who'd make it bearable. Open it eventually.

results.name: The Grid Failure
results.tagline: Everything still exists, just not together
results.blurb: You are not afraid of the disaster. You are afraid of the systems going quiet: the payment terminal, the fridge, the group chat. You'd be the one knocking on doors with a torch and a plan for who has the generator. You are at your best when the normal way stops working.
results.watchOut: You fix the systems and forget to ask whether anyone is okay. Check the people too.

results.name: The Quarantine
results.tagline: You were socially distant before it was policy
results.blurb: Your instinct is not to flee but to close ranks: a small group, a strict door, a routine. You are unusually good at the long, dull middle of a crisis, the part everyone else finds unbearable. You would keep people alive and slightly annoyed about it.
results.watchOut: You can keep the circle so small that nobody new ever gets in. Leave a gap.

results.name: The Rising Water
results.blurb: You think in gradients: how high, how fast, which road stays dry. Water is the disaster that rewards foresight and punishes sentiment, so you are quietly ruthless about what can be left behind. You will be dry, and you will feel odd about it.
strengths: Keeps a route out in mind
results.watchOut: Not everything you leave behind was clutter. Decide that on purpose.

results.name: The Machine
results.tagline: It learned from us, which was the mistake
results.blurb: Your apocalypse is the one where the thing we built keeps going without us. You are less scared of the bang than of the process nobody supervised. You'd spend the last week trying to understand it, and you would probably get further than anyone expected.
strengths: Sees the system behind the event
Finds the off switch nobody documented
results.watchOut: Understanding the machine is not the same as being needed by it. Stay human.

results.name: The Impact
results.blurb: You would rather face the clean, enormous, undeniable disaster than the slow argument. You are good in the first hour: fast decisions, no sentiment, everyone moving. The aftermath is where you get bored, because it is all logistics and no drama.
strengths: Fast and clear in the first hour
results.watchOut: After the flash comes the year of small decisions. Stay for those too.

results.name: The Ash Year
results.tagline: You'd survive the bang, not the harvest
results.blurb: You are drawn to the disaster that keeps giving: the ash, the failed crops, the sky that stays wrong for a season. You think in consequences rather than events, which makes you dull at parties and extremely useful in a crisis that refuses to end.
results.watchOut: You can prepare for the second-order disaster and miss the friend who needs you now.

results.name: The Long Winter
results.blurb: Your disaster is the one where the temperature drops and everything slows down. You are built for it: layers, patience, a stubborn refusal to waste energy on complaining. You'd be the person still functioning in month four, when everyone else has gone quiet.
strengths: Thrifty with heat, food and words
Keeps going long after the novelty
results.watchOut: Endurance is not a personality. Let someone bring you something warm.

results.name: The Quiet Fade
results.blurb: You have noticed that the end does not need to announce itself. Things stop arriving, the shelves thin out, the news moves on, and everyone keeps going to work. You would be the first to say it out loud and the last to be believed, which suits you fine.
results.watchOut: Being right early is lonely. Find the one person who'll listen.
